admitted.text: Randi seems frightened by Pace’s tenderness because being loved past her polished face threatens the defenses that keep her safe.
admitted.detail_quote: Tenderness was something the face received and passed inward, in amounts she decided.

admitted.text: She reads as a woman who has built an immaculate, high-status social persona as armor so that nothing real or unmanageable can ever touch her.
admitted.detail_quote: her thumb had found the rim of her water glass and set the edge of it in under the nail, bearing down.

admitted.text: Her eating reads as tightly policed, with refusal as reflexive as breathing.
admitted.detail_quote: Easy, automatic, not even a glance back at the tray.

admitted.text: Her desire for Vee reads as larger and more frightening to her than the game she and Pace set up allows.
admitted.detail_quote: a want too big for her face, and keeping the face over it anyway

admitted.text: Randi reads as intensely desirous of Vee while needing to disguise that hunger as a gift offered to Pace.
admitted.detail_quote: She had made herself not a woman who hungered for another woman, which he could see was unsurvivable, but a girlfriend offering her man a gift, which was merely sexy.

admitted.text: With Vee she reads as a skilled, slightly predatory confidante who draws out confessions step by step.
admitted.detail_quote: A decade of dance and three years of whatever sorority actually taught under the mixers and the letters, all of it folded down into three seconds of execution so clean it looked like nothing

admitted.text: By chapter 18 she reads as jealous and left out, hurt that Pace has Vee while she herself only gets reports.
admitted.detail_quote: You've got her all weekend, every weekend, and you're in no hurry, and I can't think why you would be.

admitted.text: Her warmth toward Vee also reads as real tenderness, especially when she reassures her.
admitted.detail_quote: Her feet did a thing on the brick, a half-second of happy footwork she didn't decide to do

admitted.text: He reads as truly devoted to consent and to letting the woman choose, almost to the point of principle.
admitted.detail_quote: She chooses it, Randi. Every step of it. Or it isn't anything.

admitted.text: Pace also reads as someone who carefully engineers situations so that another person’s freely made choice arrives inside conditions he designed.
admitted.detail_quote: he had built it. Open, everything open.

admitted.text: He seems blind to Randi's emotional state, and good at reading bodies but not hearts.
admitted.detail_quote: He took it for the want — too big for her, come down on him with nowhere else to go.

admitted.text: Pace reads as tenderly discreet, withholding Vee’s private confession even from Randi.
admitted.detail_quote: He thought of what she had said after, on the walk — the true thing she had asked him to pretend she hadn't — and did not hand it over.

admitted.text: His restraint seems shaped by an old guilt about intruding on a lover's private feelings.
admitted.detail_quote: Daphne had built a door, once, and he had not respected it.

admitted.text: His tenderness toward Vee reads as sincere rather than calculated.
admitted.detail_quote: I can't sew," she said. It came out before anything else, a reflex, a small panic.

admitted.text: Pace reads as a maker whose love language is patient construction fitted to the exact person before him.
admitted.detail_quote: He hadn't matched the dress she'd described. He'd matched her.

admitted.text: She seems to badly need being chosen, and is willing not to ask why.
admitted.detail_quote: that she had been chosen, plainly, for reasons she didn't need to understand

admitted.text: She seems to carry her mother's shaming voice inside her, and that voice has fused with her desire.
admitted.detail_quote: she could not find the seam between the heat and the shame because there was no seam, they ran on the same wire

admitted.text: Vee reads as trained to treat her abundant body and appetite as social dangers requiring constant cover.
admitted.detail_quote: The voice said *floozie* in her mother's exact word and her thighs pressed once, hard, on their own, under her jeans.

admitted.text: Her attraction to Randi reads as real but unnamed, something she covers with jokes.
admitted.detail_quote: *French,* she thought. *It's a French thing, she does the kiss-kiss, she's been everywhere, that's all it is, that's just how women like her say goodbye.*

admitted.text: She reads as overreaching with money to keep up with Randi's world, against her own careful habits.
admitted.detail_quote: the one thing she would not do at this table was let Randi buy her seat at it.

admitted.text: By the end she seems to be blossoming into confidence about being looked at.
admitted.detail_quote: There was nothing under it. She knew that even while she did it

admitted.text: She seems to be drifting from Cassie and quietly ignoring her own unease about it.
admitted.detail_quote: What she kept was the middle. She lifted it out clean as she went

admitted.text: She reads as fiercely loyal, caring about Vee herself rather than the glamour around her.
admitted.detail_quote: The whole forty seconds Vee had spent being a student, Cassie had spent watching what the dress had done to her friend, because the friend was the only part of any of it Cassie had ever been able to see.

admitted.text: She seems quietly suspicious of Randi and watches her when others don't.
admitted.detail_quote: He looked at her—" a tip of her chin toward Randi "—the way you'd look at somebody's great-aunt.

admitted.text: Cassie reads as protective without becoming possessive, repeatedly letting Vee’s evasions stand when pressing would cost trust.
admitted.detail_quote: Cassie listened with her chin on her knees and did not pull at the seam.

admitted.text: Brooke reads as a polished gatekeeper whose warmth makes social interrogation harder to resist or name.
admitted.detail_quote: The conversation was over because Brooke had decided it was over.

admitted.text: She reads as socially slippery, her friendliness capable of serving any purpose.
admitted.detail_quote: the laugh that meant nothing on its own and was therefore available for anything

admitted.text: She reads as calm and gently sceptical of new-romance certainty.
admitted.detail_quote: Everybody's different at the start.

admitted.text: She reads as an exuberant cheerleader who sees Pace's intent more plainly than Vee does.
admitted.detail_quote: He wants you for the afternoon. Bring a change of clothes.

admitted.text: He reads as a kind, rejected suitor, a benchmark of the ordinary niceness Vee has outgrown.
admitted.detail_quote: He's nice." Kayla watched Theo find a seat, mournful about it.

admitted.text: Her warmth toward Pace seems to vouch for his decency.
admitted.detail_quote: the warmth of how she'd said hello to him stayed at the table after she'd gone

admitted.text: the hidden bench: the controlled hunger and erotic purpose concealed beneath ordinary social surfaces
admitted.detail_quote: full of what it was, doing what it would continue to do, waiting for the next time.

admitted.text: The key turning in a lock: it reads as Randi locking her true self away.
admitted.detail_quote: the size of a key turning in a lock.

admitted.text: Thin apple slices: they read as Randi's portioned, rationed appetite.
admitted.detail_quote: a girl who had been portioning herself, weighing every want before she let herself have it

admitted.text: The Chi Latte sign: it reads as Vee's admission into an insiders' world.
admitted.detail_quote: the way a thing is funny only once you're allowed in on it

admitted.text: the crossed mathematical mark: separate desires becoming legible when placed together at the right angle
admitted.detail_quote: On their own these two are a struggle — you push and they won't give, and neither one quite looks like what it is. Put them together, at right angles, and they turn into a single thing that's suddenly plain

admitted.text: Simpson's paradox: it reads as the same facts telling opposite stories depending on how they are grouped.
admitted.detail_quote: Same numbers. Nobody touched one of them.

admitted.text: The burgundy silk: it reads as Pace seeing Vee herself rather than her stated wish.
admitted.detail_quote: All of her was there, gathered up and set out like it had nothing to apologize for.

admitted.text: The flannel and the sheets: they read as substitute intimacy giving way to the real thing.
admitted.detail_quote: the actual thing behind the proxy she'd been studying in her own bed

admitted.text: The folded green panties: they read as Vee's shame turned into a deliberate gift.
admitted.detail_quote: the spot exactly where she'd put it

admitted.text: Randi's untouched bowl: it reads as her refusing what Pace gives, and a hurt he can't see.
admitted.detail_quote: the one line she had drawn through it still there.

admitted.text: the pointing game: Randi’s desire disguised as play until her bare yes exposes real preference
admitted.detail_quote: the bare arrival of a thing already true before she got to it

admitted.text: the pedestal/riser: exposure reframed as being honored, the apparatus that turns shame into being seen.
admitted.detail_quote: she was no longer sure she was dry even back there

admitted.text: the expensive heels: Randi’s glamour converting Vee’s desire into debt by making extravagance feel owed
admitted.detail_quote: The shoes were not a want she had to own as a want. They were what the dress was owed.

admitted.text: What will happen when Vee learns that Randi and Pace are lovers who selected her together?
admitted.detail_quote: Both her friends turned toward her and not the professor

admitted.text: Will Randi ever come out again from behind the face she resolved to keep?
admitted.detail_quote: The one he had found was going back behind it, and she was not coming out again.

admitted.text: Why does Randi hide her Kentucky childhood, which Vee mistakes for somewhere abroad?
admitted.detail_quote: the esses ran a half-beat long, and the a's came up arched and lifted

admitted.text: What happened with Daphne, and what did it cost Pace?
admitted.detail_quote: it had cost him more than he had known, then, that anything could cost

admitted.text: What caused the large scar high on Pace’s inner thigh?
admitted.detail_quote: Something crossed him at *parents* — a small closing, there and gone, a door easing shut two rooms away.

admitted.text: Was Cassie's "Goodbye" a premonition of losing Vee?
admitted.detail_quote: And then, plainly, as she said everything: "Goodbye, Vee.

admitted.text: Will Vee's credit-card spending to keep up with Randi catch up with her?
admitted.detail_quote: she did not have the next part, the paying-it-back part

admitted.text: Will the induction go the way Vee imagines?
admitted.detail_quote: She knew that even while she did it — that she did not have the next part, the paying-it-back part, that it would be sitting there next month

admitted.text: What does the white-gold band Randi never removes mean to her?
admitted.detail_quote: And the band at her wrist — white gold, plain and heavy, no stone, nothing to it but the weight — that Vee had never once seen her without

admitted.text: Can Randi tell Pace plainly that she feels excluded and jealous before resentment turns their game cruel?
admitted.detail_quote: How long are you going to take?

admitted.text: What exactly do Randi and Pace intend to ask of Vee when their pointing game becomes a real proposition?
admitted.detail_quote: How do I get her from where she is to us, on your schedule?

admitted.text: Will Vee’s eventual choice still feel free when Randi and Pace have covertly arranged so much of the path toward it?
admitted.detail_quote: What none of them sees coming is how real it will get for each of them.
